newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 19.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- RUSH OF TAX REVENUE GIVES TORIES A LIFT

The government has been given a pre-election boost after figures from the Treasury revealed the strongest improvement in the public finances since 1989. The figures show that the government raised 5.8 billion stg more in tax revenues than it spent in January, almost twice the expected net flow into the public sector's coffers. Chancellor Kenneth Clarke said the figures confirm he is on course to hit or even come in below the 26.4 billion stg government borrowing forecast made in November's Budget.
-- VW SUSPENDS EXECUTIVES AFTER BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS

German automotive giant Volkswagen has suspended three purchasing managers following allegations in the German magazine Der Spiegel that members of the company's purchasing staff had been attempting to extract bribes from suppliers over a period of years. Following publication of the allegations executives from several of Europe's leading components companies confirmed that 'kickbacks' remain entrenched in the motor industry.
-- BRUSSELS TO PRESS CUBA LAW DISPUTE AT WTO

The European Union is expected on Wednesday to ask the World Trade Organisation to set up a disputes panel to rule on the dispute over the US Helms-Burton laws, which allows American companies to take legal action against foreign companies trafficking in Cuban assets confiscated by the Castro regime. However, the EU has also told the US that it is prepared to continue seeking an amicable settlement of the dispute despite the setting up of a WTO panel.
-- BA-AMERICAN LINK 'WILL COST PASSENGERS $500 MILLION'

A US consumer watchdog has warned that the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines could cost passengers over $500 million a year. The Consumer Federation of America, a coalition of more than 240 consumer groups, said the deal should only be approved by regulators if the two partners make substantial concessions on landing slots - demanding they cede up to 840 take-off and landing slots at Heathrow.
-- MGAM HOLDS ON TO CRUCIAL PORTFOLIO

Wellcome Trust has told troubled fund manager Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) that it wants it to continue to manage 489 million stg of its 8.5 billion stg fund. The announcement follows a review carried out by Wellcome Trust executives in the wake of the sacking of MGAM fund manager Peter Young last year and the high profile case of another fund manager, Nicola Horlick, in January. MGAM welcomed the decision as evidence that 'it is business as usual' following the two departures.
-- RECENT SELL OFFS 'GIVE BEST RETURN'

Research published on Wednesday by the Centre for the Study of Regulated Industries, an independent research organisation, will show that small private investors have benefitted from the privatisation of water and electricity companies more than from earlier government sell-offs. The study will add weight to the Labour party's arguments in favour of the proposed 'windfall tax' on the privatised utilities. The survey also reveals that private investors benefited the most from the rash of takeovers in the electricity sector.
-- GULF CANADA WINS CONTROL OF CLYDE

Canadian oil and gas group Gulf Canada Resources has succeeded in its 494 million stg hostile takeover bid for UK oil independent Clyde Petroleum. Gulf declared its offer unconditional after securing 51.42 percent of its target on Tuesday, the closing date. The indications are that the result was strongly influenced by a sale of shares by former directors, including founder and former chairman Colin Phipps.
-- ANTIDEPRESSANTS CHEER SMITHKLINE

SmithKline Beecham SBa.L, the UK's second-largest drugs company, has reported a 14 percent increase in 1996 pre-tax profits to 1.545 billion stg. The sharp rise in profits was helped by surging sales of new drug, especially antidepressants, although a strong pound hit the group's performance in the fourth quarter, SmithKline said. The company said that fourth quarter profits would have grown 23 percent if currencies had been steady instead of the 14 percent increase.
-- PEPTIDE SPENDS MORE ON R&D

Cambridge-based biotechnology company Peptide Therapeutics has reported pre-tax losses of 4.6 million stg for 1996, compared to losses of 3.6 million stg the previous year. The company said the deeper losses were due to increased spending on research and development, up to 5 million stg from 3.2 million stg. Peptide also announced details of three new drugs going into clinical trials, including vaccines for typhoid and influenza, as well as a board reshuffle.
-- COLT TELECOM MOVING AHEAD OF TARGETS

Colt Telecom has announced losses in 1996 of 11.2 million stg in its maiden results since floating in London and New York last December. Colt specialises in discount telephone services in Europe's principle financial centres, where it has a network of fibre optic connections. The company, which invested 39 million stg in capital spending last year, said it would not show a profit until early next century because of continuing heavy investment in infrastructure.
